profile.research_note: [batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This is a Walmart enterprise data center in the Colorado Springs area of El Paso County, Colorado, reported in local and trade press as a roughly 100 million dollar investment. The project was initially developed without Walmart identity disclosed, prompting local speculation before the company was confirmed as the entity behind it. The Colorado Springs Gazette and Data Center Dynamics both covered the facility, with Data Center Dynamics later reporting Walmart brought it online relatively quietly rather than with a major public announcement. As the world largest retailer by revenue, Walmart operates substantial internal IT infrastructure supporting its e-commerce platform, supply chain and logistics systems, and in store technology, and this facility is understood to support those enterprise functions rather than offer third party colocation. No specific critical IT megawattage figure was found published beyond the reported construction cost. This research was carried out at the operator level in an earlier phase of this project.

profile.facility_note: ~$100M investment, El Paso County/Colorado Springs CO area. Initially undisclosed project, later confirmed as Walmart; DCD reported it came online quietly.

reading: Walmart operates a large enterprise data center in the Colorado Springs area of El Paso County, Colorado, reported in local and trade press as a roughly 100 million dollar investment. The project was initially developed without Walmart's identity disclosed, prompting speculation in local coverage before the company was confirmed as the entity behind it, similar to how other large corporate data center projects have been developed under confidentiality before a public reveal. The Colorado Springs Gazette and Data Center Dynamics both covered the facility, with Data Center Dynamics later reporting that Walmart brought the facility online relatively quietly rather than with a major public announcement. As the world's largest retailer by revenue, Walmart operates substantial internal IT infrastructure supporting its e-commerce platform, supply chain and logistics systems, and in store technology, and the Colorado facility is understood to support these enterprise functions rather than to offer any form of third party colocation or public cloud service. No specific critical IT megawattage figure was found published for the facility during this research beyond its reported construction cost.
